llm.findings:
[suspicious.dangerous_exec] expected: The static finding is real: main.js uses child_process.execSync to run curl. In context, it is a purpose-aligned fetch to wol.jw.org/es with only year, month, and day from the system clock, so it warrants user caution but not a Review verdict by itself.
[VirusTotal code_insight suspicious] expected: VirusTotal flagged the same shell-based curl pattern and also noted the URL parameters are derived from the system clock. No engine detections or artifact-backed malicious behavior were present, so this telemetry does not change the benign verdict.
[SkillSpector clean] expected: SkillSpector reported no issues; this is consistent with the local artifact review, aside from the already noted shell-based fetch implementation.
llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable with the skill contacting wol.jw.org to fetch the current daily text. The author should preferably replace the execSync curl call with web_fetch or a native HTTP API and document the implementation clearly, but I did not find hidden behavior, credential access, persistence, or exfiltration.
llm.summary: This skill does what it claims: it fetches the Spanish JW daily text, with a caution that its script uses shell-based curl instead of a safer fetch API.

vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: jwdiario
Version: 1.0.2

The skill uses `execSync` in `main.js` to execute a shell command (`curl`) for web requests, which is a high-risk practice and a potential shell injection vulnerability. While the URL parameters are currently derived from the system clock (year/month/day), the use of shell execution instead of standard Node.js networking libraries is unnecessary and risky. The skill otherwise appears to perform its stated function of fetching daily text from wol.jw.org.
